notes.1a: Many candidates understood the role of the salivary glands and knew that ingestion involved the mouth. Egestion was sometimes confused with digestion.
notes.1b: Many candidates understood the breakdown of fats. Common incorrect responses for glycerol were glucagon or glycogen.
notes.1c: A few candidates stated the correct elements but many incorrectly stated amino acids.
notes.2a: Many candidates gave examples of transmissible diseases rather than a definition.
notes.2b: Candidates showed an excellent understanding of water treatment with the best responses providing specific details of the processes involved.
notes.2ci: This was a challenging question, while most were able to work out the decrease fewer were able to convert it to a percentage.
notes.2cii: Many candidates gave the correct type of organism.
notes.2di: This question was generally well answered, but it is important that candidates do not confuse defecation with excretion.
notes.2dii: This question was often misread, so that factually correct information was given but it did not answer the question. Responses that gave the treatment for symptoms were excellent.
notes.3a: This question was generally well answered with only a few confusing xylem and phloem. It is important that arrows do touch the actual part.
notes.3b: A really well answered question. Cambridge International General Certificate of Secondary Education 0610 Biology June 2019 (c) Many candidates were able get most of the order of size correct, with the size of chloroplast causing most difficulty.
notes.4a: This question was generally well answered. It was important to look at the arrows in the diagram carefully and decide if the arrow was pointing to the amniotic sac or its contents.
notes.4b: Many candidates were unclear about when the changes occur, so gave a lot of information on how fertilisation occurs and then development of the fetus, without detailing the bit in between.
notes.4c: Again many candidates were unclear about when changes occur. Most thought that organs developed in late pregnancy.
notes.5b: An excellent understanding of specialised cells shown.
notes.5c: Most candidates were able to show the links for the characteristics of sexual reproduction.
notes.5d: Most candidates could identify which diagrams showed asexual reproduction. A few understood the significance of one parent, rather than resulting from a single cell (which could be part of meiosis).
notes.6a: There were excellent descriptions of the data.
notes.6b: It is important to read all the information in the question. There were two sentences to be read before answering and the benefits of vaccination were not required. There were some good answers from a few candidates who focused on health and food production.
notes.6c: Excellent answers were given by many candidates.
notes.7ai: Many candidates correctly interpreted the photomicrograph, but some were unaware that vascular tissue is within the spongy mesophyll.
notes.7aii: The photomicrograph showed a very large vascular bundle and some smaller ones. A ring around any whole bundle was sufficient. Many candidates ringed only a few cells.
notes.7aiii: Better answers were given for this question, with clear arrows to the airspaces. A few confused the space inside a cell with the spaces outside.
notes.8a: Most candidates gave a correct response to this question.
notes.8b: Some candidates gave the correct response. A common error was to quote effects on livestock rather than on the ecosystem.
notes.9ai: This question was well answered by most candidates, only a few restated the results instead of the change or lack of change.
notes.9aii: Most candidates gave the correct response.
notes.9aiii: Many candidates found it challenging to describe what was happening. Cambridge International General Certificate of Secondary Education 0610 Biology June 2019 (b) There were some good answers to this question.
